title: Account Credit Deposit Credit on Redemption Restores, Domain Registrations
content:
## Training note: the deposit credit on a restore

**Which charge does this credit concern?** The amount of a redemption restore of a Domain Registrations domain billed on or after 1 December 2025. The restored-year volume credit is one of the restored-year credits of that restore.

**What is the rule?** The restored-year volume credit is USD 0.50 for each restored year where the account credit deposits posted on the customer's account less than 12 whole months before the day of the restore total USD 5000.00 or more, USD 0.25 for each restored year where they total at least USD 250.00 but less than USD 5000.00, and nothing where they total less, a month counting only once its day of the month is reached.

**Whose records decide it?** The account credit ledger of the customer's Harborline Customer Accounts account: only deposits into account credit are added up, and only those posted less than 12 whole months before the day of the restore.

**How are the 12 whole months counted?** A month is complete only once its day of the month is reached. A deposit posted on 18 March 2028 is 11 whole months old on 17 March 2029 and still counts for a restore that day; on 18 March 2029 it is 12 whole months old and no longer counts.

**Where are the band edges?**

| Deposits in the window | Credit per restored year |
|---|---|
| USD 5000.00 or more | USD 0.50 |
| USD 250.00 up to USD 4999.99 | USD 0.25 |
| Below USD 250.00 | Nothing |

Deposits of exactly USD 5000.00 fall in the top band; exactly USD 250.00 falls in the middle band; USD 249.99 earns nothing.

*Hypothetical case:* deposits of USD 400.00 and USD 120.00 inside the window total USD 520.00, so a restore of one restored year earns USD 0.25.
